# Full-course diagnostic — Week13 lesson1
Try these eight optional self-check questions, each with two ideas to explain. Allow around 30 minutes if useful, or work at your own pace. Try explaining from memory first, then use notes and explained answers to fill gaps. Combine this with your earlier Unit 3/4 work to choose what to revisit. No marks are assigned.
P1: `grid=[[0]*2]*2; grid[0][1]=7`. Give grid and explain shared-row aliasing.
P2: Binary search [3,6,9,12,15] for 12. Give mid/index trace 2 → 3, and sorted-input precondition.
P3: In insertion sort [5,2,4,2], give list after inserting the value 4, and explain why strict > retains equal-key order.
P4: Session.reserve refuses a full session; OnlineSession overrides location. Explain polymorphic location dispatch, and why `_booked` is not a security boundary or a DB constraint.
D1: Resource LEFT JOIN Loan: R04 has no loans. Explain COUNT(*) versus COUNT(LoanID), and why a preserved NULL row must not be counted as an active loan.
D2: Loan insertion then invalid Inspection.Passed = 2 fails in one explicit transaction. Explain rollback of both-step operation, and why this alone cannot demonstrate crash durability.
N1: Traditional IPv4 subnet 192.168.40.64/27. Give usable range .65–.94 and broadcast .95, and explain that a remote destination normally uses a next-hop gateway MAC on the first Ethernet segment rather than the remote server MAC.
S1: HTTPS export allowed in a hypothetical APP entity; no recipient/harm finding. Explain connection protection versus application permission, and why federal eligible-breach notification cannot be decided from this fact alone.
For each item record: independent response, criterion met/missing, likely cause, linked repair task. Choose TWO priority causes using stakes and repeated evidence, not just a grand total. If uncertainty spans all strands, teacher chooses prerequisite repairs and preserves later support needs.
